prompt.context_jp: 場の主導権を握るのは、いつものように白金大臣その人___あった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 場の主導権を握るのは、いつものように白金大臣その人___あった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in the 'X であった' identification cleft?

feedback.correct_en: The cleft '〜のは…であった' identifies who held the initiative. The copula で+あった links the two sides, so で is required here.
feedback.incorrect_en: が or は would break the cleft; 'そのひとが/はあった' doesn't form the identifying predicate.

prompt.context_jp: 「申し訳ございません わたくしの部下の働き___芳しくないようで…」
prompt.prompt_jp: わたくしの部下の働き___芳しくないようで…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the subordinate's performance as the new information being apologized for.

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is presenting new information to the minister — the subordinate's poor performance — as the subject of 芳しくない. New-information subjects of describing predicates take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a topic ('as for my subordinate's performance…'), which sounds like detached commentary, not an apology surfacing the fact.

prompt.context_jp: 「まあ 国民の命___ ひとつ助かったんだから よしとしましょう」
prompt.prompt_jp: 国民の命___ひとつ助かったんだから
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the life that was saved.

feedback.correct_en: 助かる is an intransitive change-of-state verb; the thing that gets saved is a new-information subject, naturally taking が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize 'the citizen's life' as if contrasting with something else, which doesn't match this throwaway concession.

contrast_examples.en: The life (in contrast) couldn't be saved.

prompt.context_jp: 「喜多見チーフの過去___ 気になるので 今 調べている最中です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見チーフの過去___気になるので
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle before 気になる.

feedback.correct_en: 気になる takes が for the thing that catches one's interest. Otowa is naming what newly concerns him as a stimulus.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is ungrammatical with 気になる (which is intransitive). は would mark Kitami's past as the already-established topic rather than the subject that triggers the feeling.

contrast_examples.jp: あの話は気にならない。
contrast_examples.en: That story, I'm not bothered by.

prompt.context_jp: その日の昼、比奈は病院の食堂の隅の席___ひとり腰を下ろした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 食堂の隅の席___ひとり腰を下ろした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the destination of 腰を下ろす.

feedback.correct_en: 腰を下ろす takes に for the spot one lowers oneself onto — a destination of motion.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an action in general, but here the seat is the end point of 下ろす, so に is natural.

prompt.context_jp: トレーの上には湯気を立てるトンカツ定食と豚汁が並んでいた___、箸を持つ手___なかなか動かなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 箸を持つ手___なかなか動かなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best captures the contrast between the hot food being there vs. her hand not moving?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator sets up a contrast: the food is piping hot, but her hand (はい) stubbornly won't move. は carries that contrastive 'as for her hand…' nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply report new information about the hand, losing the pointed contrast with the steaming food just mentioned.

contrast_examples.jp: 料理は熱いが、箸は動かない。
contrast_examples.en: The food is hot, but the chopsticks (contrast) don't move.

prompt.context_jp: そこへ、指導医である高輪千晶___偶然のように声をかけてきたのだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 指導医である高輪千晶___偶然のように声をかけてきた
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing Takanawa as a newly-appearing character.

feedback.correct_en: Takanawa is introduced onto the scene for the first time in this paragraph — classic new-information が. The reader doesn't yet know she's there.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose Takanawa as already-established topic, which doesn't match 'そこへ…' + first appearance.

contrast_examples.en: At that moment, the teacher appeared.

prompt.context_jp: 「おなかだけ___ すいちゃって 豚汁も つけました」
prompt.prompt_jp: おなかだけ___すいちゃって
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that pairs with だけ to add a contrastive 'at least' nuance.

feedback.correct_en: だけは is a set contrastive pattern — 'my stomach, at least, is hungry (even if nothing else feels right).' Hina is contrasting hunger with her low spirits.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would mark exclusive subject ('only my stomach is hungry'), which loses the 'at least this one thing' resignation.

contrast_examples.en: At least don't do this one thing.

prompt.context_jp: 「なんで 私___ ＭＥＲに選ばれたんでしょうか」
prompt.prompt_jp: なんで 私___ＭＥＲに選ばれたんでしょうか
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits 'why ME (and not someone else)?'

feedback.correct_en: Hina is asking why, out of many interns, SHE specifically was picked — exhaustive-listing が ('it was I who was chosen'). This is reinforced by 他にも たくさん 研修医はいます that follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は would make her the topic ('as for me, why was I chosen'), losing the 'why me specifically out of all of them' force.

contrast_examples.en: I (of all people) was the one chosen.
As for me, I was chosen.

prompt.context_jp: 「救命___ 常に人不足で激務だから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 救命___常に人不足で激務だから
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 救命 as the topic being characterized.

feedback.correct_en: Takanawa is making a general characterization of the ER department ('as for the ER, it's always understaffed'). That's prototypical topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 救命が would present it as new information or exhaustive — but Takanawa isn't introducing it, she's commenting on a known department.

prompt.context_jp: 「ミスしたんだったら 見返してやれば？ 自分___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 見返してやれば？ 自分___
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 自分 as the thing to prove something to / show up.

feedback.correct_en: 見返す here takes a direct object ('show up / prove yourself against') — Takanawa tells Hina to prove herself to herself, so 自分を.
feedback.incorrect_en: 自分が would make Hina the one doing the proving (which is already implicit in the verb). 自分に changes the sense to 'to herself' in a dative way, not idiomatic here.

prompt.context_jp: 「自分の ふがいなさに 腹___ 立ってるんだったら」
prompt.prompt_jp: 腹___立ってるんだったら
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the set phrase 腹___立つ.

feedback.correct_en: 腹が立つ is a fixed collocation for 'to feel angry' — 腹 is the grammatical subject of 立つ and takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 腹は立つ sounds like topic/contrast ('as for anger, it rises'), which is odd. 腹を立てる exists but uses a different verb form.

contrast_examples.en: I get angry at him. (transitive variant)

prompt.context_jp: 「彼女 私の前___無理に笑ってた」
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女 私の前___無理に笑ってた
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'in front of me' as location.

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action (laughing) is performed. 'In front of me' is the setting of the forced smile.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a static existence location, not an action's venue. を is ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.jp: みんなの前で発表する。

contrast_examples.en: Be in front of the station.

prompt.context_jp: 「私は大丈夫よ 大変なの___ 喜多見先生ですね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 大変なの___喜多見先生ですね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the cleft '〜のは X です'.

feedback.correct_en: The cleft pattern 〜のは X です presents X as the exhaustive identification of who is in trouble: 'the one who has it rough is Dr. Kitami.' The nominalized clause is the topic marked by は.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが大変 would make a different structure ('X is tough'), and here the sentence pivots on identifying who, so は fits the cleft.

contrast_examples.en: The one in trouble is me.

prompt.context_jp: 「これ___ 弦巻先生のミスとは いえないですね」
prompt.prompt_jp: これ___弦巻先生のミスとは いえないですね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking これ as the topic of judgment.

feedback.correct_en: The committee member is giving a verdict ABOUT this incident: 'as for this, we can't call it Dr. Tsurumaki's mistake.' Topic は fits a judgment about an already-known matter.
feedback.incorrect_en: これが would mark it as new-information subject, but everyone already knows what 'this' refers to — the case under review.

prompt.context_jp: 「一番の問題___ 重要な判断を研修医の弦巻先生に 任せてしまっていたこと___ないでしょうか」
prompt.prompt_jp: 一番の問題___重要な判断を…任せてしまっていたこと___ないでしょうか
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the two blanks in the cleft '一番の問題___…ことで___ないでしょうか'.

feedback.correct_en: The cleft identifies the biggest problem: topic は on 一番の問題, and ことではないでしょうか as a hedged 'isn't it the case that…'
feedback.incorrect_en: 一番の問題が would present it as newly introduced, but the speaker is zeroing in on the known issue. ことには does not form the needed negative question copula.

contrast_examples.jp: 問題は彼の態度ではないか。

prompt.context_jp: 「次の審査会では このダメ研修医___利用する」
prompt.prompt_jp: このダメ研修医___利用する
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the direct object of 利用する.

feedback.correct_en: 利用する is transitive and takes を for the thing/person being used. Kugayama is treating the intern as an instrument.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the intern the subject (doing the using). に would mark a different relation (target), not the thing being exploited.

prompt.context_jp: 「あなた以外に 今 その人を救える人___いませんよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: その人を救える人___いませんよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the person who can save her'.

feedback.correct_en: With the restrictive 'あなた以外に', は carries the contrastive-negation nuance: 'there's no one else who can save her.' In negative existential statements like 〜人はいない, は is standard.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜人がいない is possible, but combined with あなた以外に, は highlights the contrast ('other than you — no one'). Native usage strongly prefers は here.

contrast_examples.jp: 君以外にできる人はいない。
contrast_examples.en: There's no one but you who can do it.
There's someone who can do it. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 「今は 敵対するよりも 彼らの信頼を得て 溶け込むことを優先するべきだと ___しました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 優先するべきだと ___しました
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb Otowa uses to report his bureaucratic reasoning.

feedback.correct_en: 判断する ('to judge/decide') is the standard verb a bureaucrat/doctor uses to report a professional decision based on weighing options.
feedback.incorrect_en: 想像しました ('I imagined') is too passive and doesn't fit a decision report. 遠慮しました ('I held back') doesn't match the surrounding reasoning.

contrast_examples.jp: 総合的に判断しました。

prompt.context_jp: 「喜多見チーフにも それを ___ ていました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見チーフにも それを ___ていました
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb Hina uses: 'Kitami ___ me (saw through me).'

feedback.correct_en: 見透かす means 'to see through / see into someone's hidden intentions,' exactly what Hina feels Kitami did to her cowardice.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見送られる means to be seen off (farewell). 見下される means to be looked down on — a different nuance that doesn't match 'he perceived my inner fear'.

contrast_examples.en: I was seen off at the station.

prompt.context_jp: 「比奈先生は このままだと___ しまいます」
prompt.prompt_jp: このままだと___しまいます
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that means 'will break / crack under pressure'.

feedback.correct_en: 潰れる is the standard metaphor for a person 'breaking down' from stress or workload — intransitive, happening to Hina.
feedback.incorrect_en: 壊す and 倒す are transitive and require an object; they'd need someone/something being broken, not the subject collapsing.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見の答弁は言葉少なだったが、責任を ___ 気配は少しもなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 責任を___気配は少しもなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 責任を to mean 'evade/avoid responsibility'.

feedback.correct_en: 責任を回避する ('to evade responsibility') is a fixed collocation often used in formal/journalistic contexts, matching this courtroom-like inquiry.
feedback.incorrect_en: 責任を解決する doesn't collocate; one solves problems, not responsibility. 計算する ('calculate') makes no sense here.

prompt.context_jp: 「腹 ___ 政治家先生に尾っぽ 振れ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 腹 ___ 政治家先生に尾っぽ 振れ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb completing the idiom 腹を___ ('resolve oneself').

feedback.correct_en: 腹をくくる is a set idiom meaning 'to steel oneself / make up one's mind to face something unpleasant' — Kugayama's rough command.
feedback.incorrect_en: 腹をこわす means 'to get an upset stomach,' totally wrong register. 腹をあけて isn't an idiom.

contrast_examples.en: Steel oneself and take it on.

prompt.context_jp: 「___はやめろ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___はやめろ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose what Otowa tells Hina to stop doing.

feedback.correct_en: 言い訳はやめろ ('Stop making excuses!') is the natural reprimand matching Hina's '研修医の私には無理です' — she's deflecting with reasons.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言い方 ('way of speaking') doesn't match Otowa's frustration about her reasoning. 言い伝え ('legend') is unrelated.

prompt.context_jp: 比奈の顔から、みるみる___が引いていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: みるみる___が引いていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word completing the idiom '___が引く' meaning 'to go pale'.

feedback.correct_en: 血の気が引く is a set idiom for the blood draining from one's face in shock — exactly Hina's reaction to being told she must operate alone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息が引く isn't idiomatic in this sense. 涙が引く is non-standard; 涙 goes with 出る/あふれる/こぼれる.

contrast_examples.en: The blood drained from my face.

prompt.context_jp: 「研修医が一人でオペなんて ___ ですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 研修医が一人でオペなんて ___ですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose Kugayama's word of outrage: an intern operating alone is '___'.

feedback.correct_en: 前代未聞 ('unheard-of / unprecedented') exactly captures Kugayama's incredulity at a resident performing surgery solo.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一石二鳥 means 'two birds with one stone' (positive). 自業自得 means 'reaping what you sow' — doesn't match the shock at an unprecedented event.

prompt.context_jp: Hina says 「もう辞めたいです」. Which response from Takanawa feels most natural for a senior mentor at a casual cafeteria table?
prompt.prompt_en: Which reply best matches the warm-but-firm senpai register of this scene?

choices.text: 「それでは、辞職なさいますか？」
「辞めるのをやめてください。」

feedback.correct_en: The real line 「じゃあ 辞める？」 is deliberately casual and provocative — Takanawa tosses the choice back at Hina to shake her out of self-pity. It fits the senpai-kōhai cafeteria dynamic.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is stiff keigo appropriate for an HR office, not a lunch chat. C is awkwardly phrased and sounds like a schoolteacher scolding, missing Takanawa's challenge-you-to-decide tone.

prompt.context_jp: Takanawa confronts Kitami about Hina's state. Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'she's actually broken inside'?
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the most natural rendering.

choices.text: ホントは心が折れてるのに
ホントは心が割れてるのに
ホントは心が切れてるのに

feedback.correct_en: 心が折れる ('one's spirit snaps/breaks') is the standard idiom for emotional collapse under pressure — exactly Hina's state.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心が割れる and 心が切れる aren't established collocations for this meaning. 割れる is for cracking/shattering objects, 切れる would suggest 'running out of patience' only with 堪忍袋 etc.

prompt.context_jp: Kitami hands triage off to Hina. Which encouragement fits his terse, trusting style in the middle of chaos?
prompt.prompt_en: Which line feels most natural as Kitami's send-off?

choices.text: 「比奈先生こそが唯一それをなしうる人物であると私は確信しております」
「比奈先生、できるかどうかやってみたらどうでしょうかね」

feedback.correct_en: Short, direct, and confidence-conveying — perfect for a disaster scene where every second counts. The clipped form matches Kitami's running-off urgency.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is absurdly over-formal for a smoke-filled rescue site. C sounds tentative, which would undermine Hina's confidence just when Kitami needs to boost it.

contrast_examples.jp: やってみてはいかがでしょうか。
contrast_examples.en: Why not give it a try? (tentative)

prompt.context_jp: Otowa barks at Hina mid-triage. Which version sounds most natural as a sharp, male, in-the-moment reprimand?
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the most natural blunt-command version.

choices.text: 「お前は医者だろ だったら 全力で命を救え」
「あなたはお医者さんですよね？ でしたら全力で命をお救いになってください」
「医者なんでしょう？ そうなら命救ったらいいんじゃない？」

feedback.correct_en: Short, imperative, bluntly masculine — お前/だろ/救え captures Otowa's clipped anger at Hina's hesitation in the field.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is polite keigo wholly inappropriate for a battlefield reprimand. C is weirdly casual-indifferent, undermining the urgency Otowa wants to convey.

prompt.context_jp: Governor Akatsuka backs the team. Which phrasing sounds most natural for an executive granting authorization?
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the most natural executive-authorization line.

choices.text: 「現場の判断を信じましょう 私が許可します」
「現場の思いつきを信じましょう 私が許可を与えてあげます」
「現場の勘を信用しましょうか 許可してあげちゃいます」

feedback.correct_en: 現場の判断 ('the field's judgment') and 私が許可します are standard, authoritative phrasing fitting a governor overriding bureaucratic caution.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 思いつき ('whim'), which demeans the team she's defending. C's 信用しましょうか/許可してあげちゃいます sounds casual and condescending — wrong register for a crisis room decision.

contrast_examples.en: I'll go ahead and permit you. (casual, patronizing)
